title: Deposit Of Balance Amount After Passing Of Decree Cannot Retrospectively Revive Right To Defend Under Order XXXVII CPC: J&K&L High Court
court: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
ratio: The deposit of a balance amount after the passing of a decree cannot be construed as compliance with a conditional direction retrospectively…
summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh at Srinagar has held that the deposit of a balance amount after the passing of a decree cannot be construed as compliance with a conditional direction.

note.Facts: The plaintiffs sued for recovery of Rs 57.32 lacs under Order XXXVII CPC for electrical works allegedly executed at the MLA Hostel. The defendants deposited Rs 19.01 lacs on 26-03-2023 but the balance Rs 18.81 lacs was deposited only on 25-07-2025, after the suit had been decreed in favour of the plaintiffs on 12-08-2023.
note.Issue: Whether a deposit of the balance amount after the decree can be treated as retrospective compliance with the conditional order and thereby revive the defendants’ right to defend the suit under Order XXXVII CPC.
note.Held: The High Court dismissed the appeal, holding that the post-decree deposit cannot be construed as compliance with the condition and therefore cannot revive the right to defend; the trial court’s decree was lawful.
note.Principle: A condition imposed for leave to defend under Order XXXVII CPC must be fulfilled within the stipulated period; a later deposit does not retrospectively satisfy the condition nor revive the right to defend.
note.Provisions: Order XXXVII of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC); no specific section or case cited in the source.
note.Exam angle: CPC – Order XXXVII; test the requirement of timely compliance with conditions for leave to defend and the effect of subsequent compliance on a decree already passed.

title: Better Financial Resources No Ground To Deprive Mother Of Child's Custody: Allahabad High Court Dismisses Grandparents' Appeal
case_name: Manoj Sahlot and another v. State of U.P
ratio: The grandparents' better financial resources, by themselves, cannot be a ground for depriving the mother of the child's custody.
summary: The Allahabad High Court recently dismissed an appeal filed by a child's paternal grandparents against a Single Judge order directing that the custody of their 8-year-old grandson be handed over to his mother.

note.Facts: The mother filed a habeas corpus petition seeking custody of her 8-year-old son after the paternal grandparents allegedly detained him following the father’s death; the Single Judge ordered custody to the mother, and the grandparents appealed.
note.Issue: Whether the grandparents’ superior financial resources can be a ground to deprive the mother of custody of her minor child.
note.Held: The appeal was dismissed; the custody order in favour of the mother was upheld.
note.Principle: Better financial resources alone do not constitute a ground for taking custody away from a fit mother; the child’s welfare, age, emotional bond and continuity of care are paramount.
note.Provisions: Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956; reference to the Guardians and Wards Act (no specific section cited).
note.Exam angle: Family Law – application of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 to custody disputes; could be asked on the criteria for awarding custody and the relevance (or irrelevance) of the guardian’s financial standing.
